title: Record bm0, the destination_v70 odometry curriculum behind it, and a numpy robot runtime (surrogate run)
summary: This branch records the work from destination_v32 to bm0. destination_v33 to v70 add footfall-lookahead and forward-profile terrain inputs (terrain_v1, terrain_v2; zero on flat ground), native terrain training, and a run of curriculum and reward arms. destination_v70 replaces the actor's simulator-pose ghost with one built from leg odometry (terrain_v2_odom), so every actor input can come from the robot's IMU, joint encoders and foot contact. The sim2real adapter (a compensated actor with per-episode dynamics randomization and latent identification) found the core policy already robust within its ranges: arms a-d score 32, 32, 27 and 28 of 48 matched draws against the core's 31. A one-leg simulator was fitted to the leg stand (action delay 1-2 controls, kd 0.13-0.37, toe friction 0.45-0.6, joint friction, rotor inertia), and training can now randomize those axes. bm0 is a 278-256-256-128-18 actor distilled by DAgger from pfit1 u2000 with a delay predictor in front, on a nylon + 0.75 kg body. Under all five fitted axes it passes 19 and 20 of the 96 required cases (test seeds 20261110, 20261111) on the CPU MuJoCo surrogate: standing, most stop cases and some turns, with speed and turn-rate tracking 30-90 percent past the bounds and falls in tight arcs. src/locomotion/runtime runs such a policy with numpy alone from sensor readings. Every result here is a surrogate result; nothing is native training or native evaluation. The raw suite, adapter and fitted-check records are on Spark, reduced into results.json.
next: File the queued Spark chain (start from the native destination_v70 odometry run u1200, then predictor B, pfit1 and the bm0 distillation) as a replacement pull request; then evaluate natively with pushes and a payload shift (item 3 of the PR 93 review), add table2_v1 randomization and noise on the other inputs (item 2), and build the CAN motor and IMU loop and the foot-contact source for the robot runtime.
